title: Petroleum Systems Technician
raw_text:
8-923. MOS 923A-Petroleum Systems Technician
    a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
    b. Prerequisites. DA Circular 601 series.
    c. MOS 923A. MOS 923A is an accession MOS. The primary enlisted MOS feeders are 92F and 92L.
    d. Associated SQI.
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 8–-Instructor.
         (3) P–-Parachutist.
         (4) T–-Transition (personnel only).
         (5) Z–-Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
    e. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 for (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all warrant
officer MOS)).
    f. Qualifications.
         (1) WO1/CW2 must--
               (a) Successfully complete the Petroleum Technician Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC).
               (b) Have 20/20 correctable vision and normal color discrimination per AR 40-501.
               (c) Have normal hearing.
               (d) Be a U.S. citizen. Qualify for a security clearance of SECRET.
              (e) A physical demands rating of Moderate (Gold).
               (f) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 0120 cm, Seated Power Throw
(PT) – 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0036 shuttles in
Physical Demand Category in “Moderate” (Gold).
         (2) CW3 must--
               (a) Meet qualification described in paragraph f(1).
               (b) Successfully complete the Petroleum Technician Warrant Officer Advanced Course
(WOAC).
         (3) CW4 must--
               (a) Meet qualification described in paragraph f(2).
               (b) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Staff Course (WOSC).
         (4) CW5 must--
               (a) Meet qualification described in paragraph f(3).
               (b) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Senior Staff Course (WOSSC).
    g. Duties.
         (1) WO1/CW2--
               (a) Serves as a technician or technical manager in a narrow technical functional area,
generally at battalion or lower level organizations. Additionally, may serve in junior level position in
organizations where other senior petroleum technician(s) are assigned.
               (b) Service the technical aspects of petroleum operations.
               (c) Instruct, manage and supervise personnel within a Petroleum Supply Company
concerning petroleum policy and functional procedures.
               (d) Provide technical guidance to personnel of supported units/activities in order to establish
and maintain adequate petroleum stockage levels for mission accomplishment.
               (e) Manage the assignment of duties, spot checks work adequacy and instructs and
supervises subordinates in work techniques and procedures.
               (f) Estimate requirements for personnel, equipment, user/organizational maintenance and
repair of petroleum distribution facilities.
               (g) Review, consolidate and prepare technical reports associated with POL activities in
assigned unit. Supervise quality surveillance operation.
               (h) Assist command and staff officers in appraisals of petroleum operations. Assist in
coordination and implementation of operations, training programs, administrative matters and
communication activities.
               (i) Develop standard operating procedures and performs administrative duties related to the
petroleum operation.
         (2) CW3--
               (a) Perform duties described in paragraph g(1).
               (b) Serves as the senior petroleum technician in mid-level management positions; generally
at the material manager level in Division/COSCOM.
              (c) Serves as a team leader or member at the following:
                    1. Division, Division Material Management Center (DMMC).
                    2. Corps, Material Management Center.
                    3. Corps Support Command, Material Management Division
              (d) Serves as the commander’s senior technical advisor/analyst in all areas of petroleum
operations for the organization’s mission responsibilities.
        (3) CW4--
              (a) Performs duties described paragraphs g(2).
              (b) Serves as the senior petroleum technician in positions required advanced level staff
technical skills; generally at Corps or higher level; positions requiring independence from supervision.
              (c) Responsible for synthesizing petroleum activities with all MACOMs, integrating centers
and TRADOC schools.
              (d) Provides direct interface with Air Force, Navy and Marine Corps elements involved in
petroleum operations.
              (e) Serves in positions requiring advanced technical skills to perform duties related to test
and evaluation and the development of safety policy and doctrine.
              (f) Instructs and provides technical advice to other countries in the development and
management of their respective petroleum operation systems.
              (g) Instructs and monitors students in a service school environment.
        (4) CW5--
              (a) Performs duties as described in paragraphs g(3).
              (b) Serves as the most senior petroleum technician in positions that require unusual depth
and breadth of technical knowledge for functional training and curriculum development or major systems
integration skills.
              (c) Provides technical advice and assistance in regards to petroleum activities worldwide, to
include all aspects of training, personnel, doctrine, force structure, research and development and
requirements.
              (d) Develop, review and updates the life-cycle management of the petroleum technician’s
structure and force.
              (e) Perform duties as proponent level personnel systems integrator.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
           (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate.
           (2) Table 8-923A-1. Physical requirements.
           (3) Authorized position titles are provided in appendixes B and C. The following grades are used
to code positions into one of four definable skill levels: W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4
equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed in the following standards of grade tables:
              (a) Table 8-923A-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
              (b) Table 8-923A-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
